```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Tang_2026_tacrolimus"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Tang_2026_tacrolimus"))$description`
* Article: [Ther Drug Monit. 2026;48(4):473-480](https://doi.org/10.1097/FTD.0000000000001418)

Tang et al. modelled the link between cumulative tacrolimus exposure and the
decline in kidney function in the first year after liver transplantation. They
fitted the model in two steps in Phoenix NLME. First, a one-compartment
population PK model was fitted to routine whole-blood troughs of once-daily
modified-release tacrolimus. Then, for each patient, the empirical Bayes CL/F
was used to compute a daily AUC0-24h (daily dose / CL/F), and these were summed
over 3-month intervals to give the cumulative AUC `cAUC3mon`. The change in
eGFR over each interval was regressed on `cAUC3mon` with a direct linear model
with no intercept. The slope depends on the patient's eGFR category before
transplantation.

Trough concentrations and AUC0-24h as short-term exposure metrics, effect
compartment and indirect response models, and cumulative AUCs over 1, 2, 4 and
6 months were also tried (Supplemental Table S1). Only the final `cAUC3mon`
model is packaged here.

# Population

The analysis included 44 adult liver transplant recipients at the University of
Osaka Hospital, Japan (transplants 2010-2020): median age 56 years (range
22-69), median weight 59 kg (36.8-118), 54.5 % female, and 84.1 % living-donor
grafts (Table 1). All received once-daily modified-release tacrolimus
(Graceptor), adjusted to trough targets of 8-12 ng/mL in weeks 1-2, 6-10 ng/mL
up to month 3 and 4-8 ng/mL after that. The median observed dose was 4 mg
(0.1-32 mg). There were 3360 troughs and 3504 eGFR measurements. The
pre-transplant baseline eGFR is the mean of the last three values before
transplantation, calculated with the Japanese equation
`194 * age^-0.287 * SCr^-1.094` (times 0.739 for women).

# Source trace

| Item | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Structure: one-compartment, first-order absorption, no lag | -- | Methods 'Population PK Model' |
| `lka` | log(0.19) 1/h, held constant | Table 2; Methods (from Lu 2019, reference 8) |
| `lcl` | log(23.46) L/h | Table 2 |
| `lvc` | log(1607.81) L | Table 2 |
| `e_pod_cl` | 1.68 on (min(POD, 14) / 14) | Table 2 and footnote |
| `e_hct_cl` | -0.59 on (HCT / 30) | Table 2 and footnote |
| `etalcl`, `etalvc` | SD 0.62, 0.71; correlation 0.47 | Table 2 (footnote: omega is an SD) |
| `addSd` | 3.04 ng/mL | Table 2, PK block |
| Structure: change in eGFR = Slope x cAUC3mon | -- | Results 'Population PK/PD Model'; Supplemental Figure S2 |
| `slope` | -0.59 mL/min/1.73 m^2 per mg*h/L | Table 2 (magnitude), Results text and Table 2 footnote (sign) |
| `e_renalimp_mild_slope` | -0.68 | Table 2 |
| `e_renalimp_mod_slope` | -1.14 | Table 2 |
| `e_renalimp_sev_slope` | -0.92 | Table 2 |
| `etaslope` | SD 0.20, additive | Table 2; Results ('additive IIV model') |
| `addSd_egfrcfb` | 15.41 mL/min/1.73 m^2 | Table 2, PK/PD block |
| cAUC = sum of daily dose / CL/F (state `cauc`) | -- | Methods 'Population PK/PD Model' |

# Virtual cohort

Every simulation below uses one cohort of 200 patients, 50 in each
pre-transplant eGFR category. The paper does not report how its 44 patients
were split across the categories, so equal arms are used.

Each patient takes a fixed once-daily dose drawn from a log-normal
distribution around the cohort median of 4 mg, rounded to 0.5 mg and kept
between 0.5 and 15 mg. In the clinic the dose was titrated to trough targets,
so this cohort has a wider exposure range than the real one. It is a
stress test of the model, not a copy of the study. Hematocrit is constant for
each patient and drawn around the cohort median of 28.7 %. Dosing starts on
post-operative day 1 (time 0) and lasts 365 days. `POD` counts up by one each
day.

```{r cohort}
set.seed(2026)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(2026)

arms <- c("eGFR >= 90", "eGFR 60 to <90", "eGFR 30 to <60", "eGFR <30")
n_per_arm <- 50
cohort <- tibble(
  id = seq_len(n_per_arm * length(arms)),
  arm = factor(rep(arms, each = n_per_arm), levels = arms),
  HCT = pmin(pmax(rnorm(n_per_arm * length(arms), 28.7, 5), 14), 50),
  dose_mg = pmin(pmax(round(2 * exp(rnorm(n_per_arm * length(arms), log(4), 0.5))) / 2, 0.5), 15)
) |>
  mutate(
    RENALIMP_MILD = as.integer(arm == "eGFR 60 to <90"),
    RENALIMP_MOD = as.integer(arm == "eGFR 30 to <60"),
    RENALIMP_SEV = as.integer(arm == "eGFR <30")
  )

n_days <- 365
interval_h <- 24 * n_days / 4 # four 3-month intervals
dose_times <- 24 * (seq_len(n_days) - 1)
trough_times <- dose_times + 23.9
rich_times <- 24 * 359 + 0:24 # day 360 dosing interval
boundary_times <- interval_h * 0:4
obs_times <- sort(unique(c(trough_times, rich_times, boundary_times)))

make_events <- function(subject) {
  doses <- tibble(time = dose_times, evid = 1L, amt = subject$dose_mg, cmt = "depot", dvid = NA_integer_)
  # The model has two endpoints (Cc and egfrcfb); observation rows name the
  # ODE state plus dvid = 1, and every endpoint column is returned on each row.
  obs <- tibble(time = obs_times, evid = 0L, amt = 0, cmt = "central", dvid = 1L)
  bind_rows(doses, obs) |>
    arrange(time, desc(evid)) |>
    mutate(
      id = subject$id,
      POD = floor(time / 24) + 1,
      HCT = subject$HCT,
      RENALIMP_MILD = subject$RENALIMP_MILD,
      RENALIMP_MOD = subject$RENALIMP_MOD,
      RENALIMP_SEV = subject$RENALIMP_SEV
    )
}
events <- bind_rows(lapply(split(cohort, cohort$id), make_events))
```

# Simulation

```{r simulate}
mod <- readModelDb("Tang_2026_tacrolimus")
sim <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod, events = events, returnType = "data.frame") |>
  select(id, time, Cc, auc_central, cauc, egfrcfb, cl, slope_i) |>
  left_join(select(cohort, id, arm, dose_mg), by = "id")

typ_mod <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod)
# Each subject keeps its own dose and hematocrit with the random effects at
# zero; rxode2 warns that a multi-subject solve has no omega, which is the
# intent here. Only that message is muffled.
sim_typ <- withCallingHandlers(
  rxode2::rxSolve(typ_mod, events = events, returnType = "data.frame"),
  warning = function(w) {
    if (grepl("without 'omega'", conditionMessage(w))) invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
  }
) |>
  select(id, time, Cc, auc_central, cauc, egfrcfb, cl, slope_i) |>
  left_join(select(cohort, id, arm, dose_mg), by = "id")
```

## Typical slopes against the paper's footnote

The Table 2 footnote prints the slope for each pre-transplant eGFR category:
-0.59, -0.19, 0.08 and -0.05 mL/min/1.73 m^2 per mg*h/L. With the random
effects set to zero, the packaged model's `egfrcfb / cauc` gives these
values. The Results text says that "an increase of 10 mg h/L in the cAUC3mon
resulted in a decrease of 5.9 mL/min/1.73 m^2" in the reference group.

```{r slopes}
slope_chk <- sim_typ |>
  filter(time > 0) |>
  group_by(arm) |>
  summarise(model_slope = mean(egfrcfb / cauc), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(paper_slope = c(-0.59, -0.19, 0.08, -0.05))
slope_chk |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Pre-transplant eGFR" = arm,
    "Model slope" = model_slope,
    "Table 2 footnote" = paper_slope
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 4)

stopifnot(
  # The footnote rounds to two decimals.
  all(abs(round(slope_chk$model_slope, 2) - slope_chk$paper_slope) < 1e-9),
  # Results: 10 mg*h/L lowers eGFR by 5.9 in the reference group.
  abs(10 * slope_chk$model_slope[1] - (-5.9)) < 1e-9
)
```

## Cumulative AUC: the paper's definition

The paper computed each day's AUC0-24h as daily dose / individual CL/F and
summed these over the interval. The model carries this sum in the state
`cauc`: after each once-daily dose it accumulates dose / (24 x CL/F) for
24 hours. Over the first 3-month interval it should equal the sum of
dose / CL/F over the days, with CL/F taken on each day at that day's POD.

```{r cauc-closed-form}
first_interval <- sim |>
  filter(time == interval_h) |>
  select(id, arm, dose_mg, cauc, auc_central)
# The paper's metric: the sum over the days of the interval of dose / CL/F,
# with CL/F read once per day (POD and HCT are constant within a day).
cl_daily <- sim |>
  filter(time %in% trough_times, time < interval_h) |>
  group_by(id) |>
  summarise(auc_paper = sum(first(dose_mg) / cl), .groups = "drop")
first_interval <- left_join(first_interval, cl_daily, by = "id") |>
  mutate(
    pct_diff = 100 * (cauc - auc_paper) / auc_paper,
    pct_integral = 100 * (auc_central - cauc) / cauc
  )
summary(first_interval$pct_diff)
# The last day of the interval is only partly counted (91.25 days), so the
# two differ by less than one day's increment; same drawn parameters.
stopifnot(all(abs(first_interval$pct_diff) < 1))
```

The paper's cAUC is not the integral of the concentration. `auc_central`
carries the integral. At steady state the two give the same daily increment,
because the AUC over one dosing interval equals dose / CL/F. Day 360 is used
for this check. A subject with low clearance and high volume has a half-life
of several weeks, so the check uses the median and the 90th percentile, not
the worst case.

```{r auc-steady-state}
auc_day360 <- sim |>
  filter(time %in% range(rich_times)) |>
  group_by(id) |>
  summarise(
    auc_model = diff(auc_central),
    auc_paper = diff(cauc),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (auc_model - auc_paper) / auc_paper)
summary(auc_day360$pct_diff)
stopifnot(
  abs(median(auc_day360$pct_diff)) < 0.5,
  quantile(abs(auc_day360$pct_diff), 0.9) < 2
)
```

Over the first two post-operative weeks the two diverge widely. The
`(POD / 14)^1.68` term makes CL/F very small on the first days (about 1 % of
the typical value on POD 1). Each early dose then adds a large dose / CL/F,
while the concentration is still building up slowly in the large apparent
volume. Over the first 3-month interval, the concentration integral in this
cohort is a median of `r round(median(first_interval$pct_integral), 0)` %
different from the paper's cAUC.
The slope was estimated against the paper's cAUC, so `cauc` drives the eGFR
output.

# Replicate published figures

## Figure 1: trough concentrations over the first year

The paper shows a prediction-corrected VPC. Here the plot shows the simulated
troughs, with residual error, at the cohort's own fixed doses. The trough rises
over the first two weeks, while CL/F is still low because of the
`(POD / 14)^1.68` term. It then settles at the steady-state level. That level is
about 5 ng/mL at the median prediction-corrected trough in Figure 1B.

```{r fig1, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5}
troughs <- sim |>
  filter(time %in% trough_times) |>
  mutate(Cobs = Cc + rnorm(n(), 0, 3.04))
trough_summary <- troughs |>
  group_by(time) |>
  summarise(
    p05 = quantile(Cobs, 0.05),
    p50 = quantile(Cobs, 0.5),
    p95 = quantile(Cobs, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
ggplot(trough_summary, aes(time)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = pmax(p05, 0.1), ymax = p95), fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_line(aes(y = p50), colour = "steelblue4") +
  scale_y_log10(limits = c(0.1, 1000)) +
  labs(
    x = "Time after the first dose (h)",
    y = "Tacrolimus trough (ng/mL)",
    caption = "Replicates the layout of Figure 1B of Tang 2026: simulated median and 5th-95th percentiles."
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

The paper's typical patient (4 mg/day, POD >= 14, HCT 30 %) has a
steady-state average concentration of dose / (CL/F x 24 h):

```{r typical-css}
css_typ <- 4 / (23.46 * 24) * 1000
css_typ
```

For comparison, Table 1 gives a median observed trough of 7.3 ng/mL.

## Figure 2: change in eGFR against cAUC3mon

For each subject and each 3-month interval, the change in eGFR is the slope
times that interval's cumulative AUC, plus the additive residual error. Because
the model is linear with no intercept, the change over an interval is the
difference in `egfrcfb` between the end and start of that interval, and the
interval's cAUC3mon is the difference in `cauc`.

```{r fig2, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 5}
intervals <- sim |>
  filter(time %in% boundary_times) |>
  arrange(id, time) |>
  group_by(id, arm) |>
  mutate(
    cauc3mon = cauc - lag(cauc),
    d_egfr_ipred = egfrcfb - lag(egfrcfb)
  ) |>
  filter(!is.na(cauc3mon)) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(d_egfr_obs = d_egfr_ipred + rnorm(n(), 0, 15.41))

# The difference of egfrcfb over an interval is exactly the slope times
# that interval's cumulative AUC (same drawn parameters; numerical error only).
stopifnot(all(abs(intervals$d_egfr_ipred - intervals$slope_i * intervals$cauc3mon) < 1e-6))

summary(intervals$cauc3mon)

bins <- c(0, 10, 20, 35, 60, Inf)
vpc2 <- intervals |>
  mutate(bin = cut(cauc3mon, bins)) |>
  group_by(bin) |>
  summarise(
    cauc = median(cauc3mon),
    p05 = quantile(d_egfr_obs, 0.05),
    p50 = quantile(d_egfr_obs, 0.5),
    p95 = quantile(d_egfr_obs, 0.95),
    n = n(),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
ggplot(intervals, aes(cauc3mon, d_egfr_obs)) +
  geom_point(aes(colour = arm), alpha = 0.4, size = 1) +
  geom_line(data = vpc2, aes(cauc, p50), linewidth = 1) +
  geom_line(data = vpc2, aes(cauc, p05), linetype = "dashed") +
  geom_line(data = vpc2, aes(cauc, p95), linetype = "dashed") +
  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 150), ylim = c(-100, 100)) +
  labs(
    x = "cAUC3mon (mg h/L)",
    y = "Change in eGFR (mL/min/1.73 m^2)",
    colour = "Pre-transplant eGFR",
    caption = "Replicates Figure 2 of Tang 2026: simulated interval changes with 5th, 50th and 95th percentiles."
  ) +
  theme_bw()
knitr::kable(vpc2, digits = 1)
```

Figure 2 of the paper has most intervals between 0 and 50 mg*h/L, a median
change near 0 at low cAUC3mon falling to about -15 mL/min/1.73 m^2 near
50 mg*h/L, and 5th-95th percentiles of roughly -50 to +40 mL/min/1.73 m^2. The
simulated percentiles here also include the three pre-transplant categories
with flatter or positive slopes, in equal shares, which is an assumption (see
below).

## Typical eGFR decline over the year by pre-transplant eGFR

```{r egfr-time, fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4}
sim_typ |>
  filter(time %in% trough_times) |>
  group_by(arm, time) |>
  summarise(egfrcfb = median(egfrcfb), .groups = "drop") |>
  ggplot(aes(time / 24, egfrcfb, colour = arm)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(
    x = "Days after transplantation",
    y = "Typical change in eGFR (mL/min/1.73 m^2)",
    colour = "Pre-transplant eGFR",
    caption = "Median over the cohort's doses and hematocrit, random effects set to zero."
  ) +
  theme_bw()
```

# PKNCA validation

NCA over the day-360 dosing interval for each pre-transplant eGFR arm. The PK
does not depend on the arm, so the arms differ only by chance. The paper
reports no NCA, so there is no published table to compare against. Instead, the
check below compares the PKNCA AUC0-24 with dose / CL/F, which is the paper's
own AUC0-24h.

```{r pknca}
# rich_times starts at the day-360 dose, so the interval has its time-0 record
conc_nca <- sim[sim$time %in% rich_times, ] |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  mutate(time_nca = time - min(rich_times)) |>
  select(id, arm, time = time_nca, Cc)
dose_nca <- cohort |>
  transmute(id, arm, time = 0, amt = dose_mg)

conc_obj <- PKNCAconc(conc_nca, Cc ~ time | arm + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCAdose(dose_nca, amt ~ time | arm + id)
intervals_nca <- data.frame(
  start = 0, end = 24,
  cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, cmin = TRUE, auclast = TRUE, cav = TRUE
)
nca_res <- pk.nca(PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals_nca))
summary(nca_res)

auc_nca <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD == "auclast") |>
  select(id, auclast = PPORRES) |>
  left_join(select(auc_day360, id, auc_paper), by = "id") |>
  mutate(pct_diff = 100 * (auclast / 1000 - auc_paper) / auc_paper)
summary(auc_nca$pct_diff)
stopifnot(
  # Linear-up/log-down trapezoids on an hourly grid against the exact
  # steady-state integral: within a few percent.
  abs(median(auc_nca$pct_diff)) < 2,
  quantile(abs(auc_nca$pct_diff), 0.9) < 5
)
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Omega scale.** The Table 2 footnote defines omega as the standard
  deviation of the IIV. The row `omega CL,V = 0.47` is therefore read as a
  correlation. As a covariance of two SDs (0.62 and 0.71) it would imply a
  correlation of 1.07, which is impossible. Phoenix NLME normally reports
  variances, and reading the diagonals as variances would also be consistent
  (0.47 would then be a covariance with correlation 0.71). The footnote's
  reading was chosen. Figure 1B supports it: at steady state, the predicted
  95th percentile of the prediction-corrected trough is about 3.2 times the
  median (about 16 against 5 ng/mL). With CL/F SD 0.62 plus the 3.04 ng/mL
  additive error, this ratio is about 2.8; with SD sqrt(0.62) = 0.79 it is
  about 3.5. The slope's omega (0.20) is read as an SD too.
* **Sign of the slope.** Table 2 prints theta Slope as 0.59. The Results
  ("The population estimate of the slope was -0.59") and the Table 2 footnote
  give the negative sign. The packaged `slope` is -0.59 and the category effects
  enter as `slope * (1 + theta)`. This reproduces all four footnote slopes.
* **Position of the slope IIV.** The additive eta is added after the
  covariate effect. The paper does not say whether it enters before or after
  the `(1 + theta)` factor.
* **cAUC.** The paper summed daily dose / CL/F, with CL/F from each
  patient's empirical Bayes estimates. CL/F depends on post-operative day and
  hematocrit, so "individual clearance" is read as that day's
  covariate-adjusted CL/F. The paper does not say this explicitly. `cauc`
  reproduces this sum for once-daily dosing, the paper's only regimen. It adds
  dose / CL/F for the most recent dose over the following 24 hours. It does
  not handle twice-daily dosing, where only the last dose would be counted.
  The concentration integral `auc_central` is also provided, but it is not
  the exposure the slope was estimated against.
* **Interval structure.** The paper fitted the change in eGFR over each 3-month
  interval against that interval's cAUC3mon. The change over the first interval
  is measured from the pre-transplant baseline. `egfrcfb` is the change from
  time 0 (the start of AUC accumulation). For a later interval, take the
  difference of `egfrcfb` at the interval's end and start. Because the model is
  linear with no intercept, this is exactly the model's prediction for that
  interval. The residual error (15.41) applies to a single interval's change.
* **POD = 0.** The `(POD / 14)^1.68` term is zero at POD 0, which gives zero
  clearance. Supply `POD >= 1`.
* **Cohort.** The doses are fixed rather than titrated to trough targets as in
  the clinic, and the pre-transplant eGFR categories are equal in size. Neither
  distribution is reported in the paper. Hematocrit is constant within a
  subject, although it varies over time in the real data.
* **Errata.** No erratum or correction was found in Europe PMC (checked
  2026-11-14).
